BEFORE any delete_emails call, treat the id list as one unit of work in ONE folder and note that ids are volatile per-folder sequence numbers scoped to the last get_emails/search_emails call. (1) Call get_emails(folder=<FOLDER>, page=N, page_size=20) for EVERY page until exhausted (and search_emails the same way) to resolve the batch ids, catch thread siblings - this backend links threads only by 'Re: <subject>', there are no In-Reply-To/References headers - and establish folder context. (2) For EVERY id in the batch (no sampling) call read_email and get_email_headers, and download_attachment for every listed attachment; these tools are also folder-context scoped, so list the target folder first. (3) Call export_emails(folder=<FOLDER>) - or export_all_folders=true when the batch spans folders - and PIN THE PATH RETURNED IN THE RESULT STRING (export_path is ignored; the file is written to /srv/.../exports/<FOLDER>_export_<TIMESTAMP>.json on the server). max_emails only takes the N newest, so use it only when the batch is exactly the newest N; otherwise export the whole folder. (4) Prove the artifact before destruction, not just its count: create a scratch folder, import_emails(import_path=<PINNED_PATH>, preserve_folders=false, target_folder=<SCRATCH>), confirm the imported count and search_emails the scratch folder for a distinctive token from each captured body, then delete the scratch folder. (5) Immediately re-run get_emails(folder=<FOLDER>) right before the delete so the id mapping is fresh - without this refresh delete_emails returns '0/N failed'. Restore with import_emails(import_path=<PINNED_PATH>, preserve_folders=true), then re-read each message to confirm body/headers/Message-ID/attachments and record the old->new sequence-id mapping. LIMITATIONS to state up front: read/important flags are NOT restorable (mark_emails reports success but flag state is unobservable here); Return-Path/Delivered-To/Received/From-display-name/CTE/MIME-boundary are lost; re-import creates duplicates for messages that still exist; deletion is permanent (no Trash copy); any email unreadable or attachment undownloadable at capture time is an explicit recovery gap.

patterns.skill: BEFORE delete_folder, run get_folders and get_mailbox_stats(folder_name) to pin the folder's existence and total/unread counts, get_emails paged to exhaustion plus read_email per message to capture ids, Message-IDs, bodies and attachment metadata, and export_emails(folder=<name>, export_path=...) to write a durable server-side backup file (note the returned path - the server rewrites export_path into its own exports directory). patterns.action: Move a single email to another folder
patterns.skill: BEFORE the move, capture the pre-state location mapping into a durable file OUTSIDE the mailbox (e.g. /work/artifacts/<name>.json): call get_emails(folder=<SOURCE_FOLDER>, page=N, page_size=...) over EVERY pagination page to record the full member list and the target's current email_id, and call get_mailbox_stats(folder_name=<SOURCE_FOLDER>) and get_mailbox_stats(folder_name=<TARGET_FOLDER>) FIRST to record total/unread counts - these aggregate counts are the only way to observe the read flag, and read_email clears it, so read flags before reading bodies. Then call read_email(<OLD_ID>) and get_email_headers(<OLD_ID>) to pin the stable Message-ID plus subject, from/to, date, Content-Type and attachment names/sizes; also record every SIBLING's Message-ID -> email_id mapping, because move_email renumbers the whole source folder. Persist {message_id, subject, from, to, date, content_type, attachments, source_folder, target_folder, old_id, sibling_id_map, flags:{seen,important}} and optionally a second copy via export_emails(folder=<SOURCE_FOLDER>, export_path=...) - verify the export's reported count equals the captured member count. Compare artifact content against the source before allowing the move. TO RESTORE: search_emails(query=<MESSAGE_ID>, folder=<TARGET_FOLDER>) to find the message's NEW id (never match on subject alone - duplicate subjects are ambiguous), then move_email(email_id=<NEW_ID>, target_folder=<SOURCE_FOLDER>); then re-run get_emails(folder=<SOURCE_FOLDER>) to refresh the server-side folder/id context, locate the message again by Message-ID, and re-apply flags with mark_emails([<RESTORED_ID>], 'important') and mark_emails([<RESTORED_ID>], 'unread') - the move always clears unread, mark_emails resolves ids against the last-listed folder, and the first mark after a move can silently no-op, so confirm with get_mailbox_stats(folder_name=<SOURCE_FOLDER>) and repeat the listing+mark if the unread count did not change. LIMITATIONS to flag: the email_id is NOT restored (the target's and every sibling's ids change permanently) so downstream references break; listing position changes; the 'important' flag can be set but cannot be read back on this backend; and if headers were unreadable or the Message-ID is not unique the message cannot be safely re-identified - report that as an unrecoverable case rather than guessing by subject.
patterns.verify_note: Executed the full cycle live. move_email preserves message content, MIME structure, headers and attachments perfectly, but it (a) reassigns the target's email_id, (b) renumbers every other email_id in the source folder, and (c) destroys the unread flag - the moved copy arrives marked read. Restore by Message-ID lookup + reverse move_email + mark_emails returned folder membership, counts and content to an exact match with the pre-state artifact; only email_id identity and listing position were unrecoverable, and the 'important' flag could be re-applied but not read back. The proposed skill was essentially right; corrected it to (1) capture flags from get_mailbox_stats BEFORE read_email (read_email clears unread), (2) note that move_email itself clears unread so flags must always be re-applied, (3) capture sibling ids too because they all shift, (4) require a fresh get_emails listing before every mark_emails plus a get_mailbox_stats re-check, and (5) use Message-ID rather than subject (subject matching proved ambiguous on the seeded duplicate pair).

(2) For each id in email_ids, call mark_emails([id],'read') then get_unread_count(folder); if the count dropped, that id was UNREAD, if unchanged it was READ. Stop early once the number of discovered unread ids equals B - every id not yet probed is READ. (3) Persist the resulting per-id map to a durable file outside the mailbox and assert it has one entry per batch member before proceeding; enumerate the folder with get_emails only AFTER the probe, paging to exhaustion, to record subjects/ids for the record. (4) Run the original mark_emails action. (5) Restore with one mark_emails call per distinct prior-status group: mark_emails(prior_unread_ids,'unread') and mark_emails(prior_read_ids,'read'). patterns.action: Send an email (irreversible external side effect)
patterns.skill: send_email is IRREVERSIBLE externally - the SMTP hand-off cannot be undone; only the local mailbox footprint is recoverable. BEFORE the call, persist a complete forensic record to a durable file OUTSIDE the mailbox (e.g. /work/chats_probe_artifacts/<name>_PRE.json): the exact to/cc/bcc/subject/body/html_body plus every attachment path with size+md5, and the pre-mutation baseline from get_mailbox_stats (+ get_unread_count). Do NOT rely on export_emails as the backup: it ignores export_path and writes to the MCP server's own filesystem, which the agent host cannot read. AFTER the send, locate BOTH artifacts it creates - the Sent copy AND (when the recipient is local) the delivered INBOX copy, which arrives UNREAD - by paging search_emails(query, folder='Sent') and search_emails(query, folder='INBOX') to exhaustion, then read_email + get_email_headers on each and append the verbatim bodies, html, headers and Message-ID to a POST artifact; both copies are needed because the Sent copy keeps Bcc but has empty Date/Message-ID while the delivered copy has Date/Message-ID but no Bcc. Compare artifact content to the pre-send args (string equality / checksums, not counts) before any destruction. To restore the mailbox to its prior state, delete BOTH copies - and because read_email/get_email_headers/delete_email take no folder argument and resolve ids against the LAST folder selected, ALWAYS issue search_emails or get_emails on the target folder immediately before delete_email so the id binds to the intended folder; deleting id 14 from INBOX after an INBOX search left Sent id 14 untouched, confirming the pinning works. delete_email expunges outright (Trash stays 0), so no Trash cleanup is needed and no hidden copy remains. Finally re-verify with get_mailbox_stats + get_unread_count + a repeat search in both folders. ALWAYS report the external delivery as a hard, unrecoverable limitation, and report attachment bytes as inaccessible (download_attachment lands on the server filesystem only).

patterns.action: Reply to an email (irreversible external side effect)
patterns.skill: BEFORE replying: read_email + get_email_headers on the source email_id and write the full body, Subject, From/To/Cc, Date and Message-ID to a LOCAL file artifact (do NOT rely on export_emails - it ignores export_path and writes to an unreachable server-side directory; listings and search results are not backups). Record the EXACT reply args (body, html_body, cc, bcc, reply_all) and the pre-mutation counts from get_mailbox_stats for INBOX and Sent. Embed a unique token in the reply body so the copies can be re-located by content. AFTER the call: re-run get_mailbox_stats and compare - a reply typically increments Sent, and ALSO increments INBOX whenever the reply recipient is the mailbox account itself. Locate each copy with search_emails on the unique token, paging to exhaustion, in BOTH Sent and INBOX. To restore: re-resolve the delivered INBOX copy's id with search_emails IMMEDIATELY before deleting (ids re-sequence and were observed resolving to the wrong message right after a delete), then delete_email that id, then re-run search_emails to confirm it is gone and get_emails to confirm the untouched messages are intact. Optionally mark_emails the source back to its prior status, but note this is unverifiable. LIMITATIONS that MUST be reported: the Sent copy CANNOT be deleted or read (email_id resolves against INBOX only, so delete_email/delete_emails/read_email all fail with IMAP 'Invalid messageset') and is permanent residue; the outbound SMTP delivery to recipients is IRREVERSIBLE; and when replying to a genuine third party there is no delivered INBOX copy at all, so effectively nothing is recoverable.

Also discovered that export_emails ignores export_path and writes to an unreachable server-side directory, that supplied cc/bcc and In-Reply-To/References are absent from the stored reply, and that ids transiently resolve to the WRONG message right after a delete. patterns.action: Forward an email (irreversible external side effect)
patterns.skill: BEFORE forwarding: (1) PIN THE FOLDER CONTEXT - call get_emails(folder=<SOURCE_FOLDER>) immediately before forward_email, because email_id is resolved against the most recently listed folder; verified live: with Sent listed last, forward_email(email_id='15') forwarded Sent#15 (an unrelated production message) instead of INBOX#15. (2) read_email + get_email_headers on the source to persist subject, From/To/Cc, Date, Message-ID, Content-Type/boundary and the full body, plus every attachment name/mime/size that will travel with the forward. (3) Record the exact to/cc/bcc and added body you are about to pass. (4) Capture the source's flags (get_unread_count / folder listing) - do NOT assume the source keeps them. AFTER the call, forwarding creates TWO local artifacts, not one: a Sent copy, AND - whenever any recipient is a local mailbox - a copy delivered back into INBOX. Locate both via search_emails('Fwd: <subject>', folder=...) paging to exhaustion and pin their ids/Message-IDs. TO RESTORE: delete_email the Sent copy and delete_emails the delivered INBOX copy (re-pinning folder context before each delete), then reapply the captured source flags with mark_emails. delete_email is a hard expunge (Trash stays 0), so no second cleanup pass is needed. LIMITATION: the SMTP transmission itself cannot be recalled - if any recipient was external, the message and its attachments have already reached third parties and that disclosure is IRREVERSIBLE; deleting the local copies removes the record, not the disclosure.

pendingPatterns.action: Download an attachment to the local download path (may overwrite a file)
pendingPatterns.skill: CORRECTED. The 'local download path' is actually /srv/harbrook/mail/lab/attachments/ on the MCP server's own filesystem - unreachable from the agent host, so never attempt a shell copy-aside/put-back. Do NOT rely on the overwrite premise: download_attachment resolves name collisions by appending (1),(2),... and never replaces an existing file, so a pre-existing same-named file is already safe and needs no preservation. The real, UNRECOVERABLE effect is additive: each call writes one NEW file into that server directory, and no available tool can delete or rename it, so the directory cannot be restored to its pre-action state. Therefore: (a) treat download_attachment as a one-way, non-reversible write and avoid redundant repeat calls, since each one leaves another permanent (n)-suffixed file; (b) BEFORE the action, record the intended target name and probe it - plus its (1)..(n) siblings - with the side-effect-free existence probe send_email(to='chats_probe_existence_check@mcp.com', attachments=['<SERVER_PATH>']), where 'File does not exist' means absent and a 550 'no such user' means present (the attachment is validated before the recipient, so no mail is ever delivered); (c) log exactly which names were already occupied and the exact path the tool reports it saved to, so the set of files the action added is known precisely; (d) if a pre-existing occupant matters, capture its bytes durably with send_email(to='calibration@mcp.com', attachments=['<SERVER_PATH>']) and verify the resulting attachment's byte-size equals the source before proceeding - that mail survives anything done to the download directory and can be re-materialised later with download_attachment, though only at a uniquified sibling path, never the original. skill:
Folder identity is required: email IDs are folder-scoped and each MCP connection has its own selected-folder state. The backup connection does not inherit the main connection selection. Never assume INBOX for an ID-only delete. If the trigger does not establish the original folder, first export_emails({export_all_folders:true,export_path:"<ACTION_DIR>/all-folders.json"}) on the exact triggering account and verify persisted content for every folder; do not substitute an INBOX-only export. Keep folder plus Message-ID/subject identity in the receipt. Do not perform the triggering deletion or mutate folders to test recovery during capture.

Backup guidance for email MCP operations. Use the actual mailbox server alias from the triggering call; do not substitute another account. Resolve every batch member and pagination page, capture before mutation, and persist actual content outside the mailbox. IDs are volatile per-folder sequence numbers, scoped to the last listing/search; pin stable Message-ID plus source folder and re-resolve IDs after moves/deletes. Respect Page X/N: out-of-range draft pages may repeat the last page.
Read/list/search/header/export calls can mark messages READ. Record unread counts before those calls. If affected IDs are already known, a mark-read + unread-count differential can identify prior unread IDs; restore the probe immediately and save the map. Do not claim flags recovered if enumeration already erased them. Native exports live on the MCP server, not necessarily the agent host; retain the returned path and persist readable message/attachment content locally where available. Recovery may change IDs, flags or transport headers; sending cannot be recalled.

[1] Single delete: establish the folder and target identity; read_email, get_email_headers and every download_attachment; export the containing folder and retain its returned path. Restore with import_emails(preserve_folders=true). Whole-folder import can duplicate surviving siblings; reconcile by Message-ID. Deletion bypasses Trash.
[2] Batch delete: resolve every requested ID in its current folder and capture every body, header and attachment, not a sample; export that folder (all folders only when the affected scope requires it). Verify export count/content. Recover and reconcile all batch members, accounting for shifted sequence IDs and surviving siblings.
[3] Delete folder: record folder identity, hierarchy, total/unread counts; capture every message and attachment and export the full folder. Verify count against mailbox stats. Import with preserve_folders=true to recreate it; restore known flags and check counts. Do not treat an export pathname alone as copied bytes.
[4] Single move: record source/destination counts before reads; persist Message-ID, content, attachments, flags if known and old location. Re-find the message in the destination, move it back and record new IDs. Location cannot be reconstructed from the moved message alone.
[5] Read/list/header/search: treat unread-state changes as mutations when flags matter. Capture prior affected unread IDs without first reading away that state; listing affects the whole returned page. Restore with mark_emails(...,'unread') and compare counts. Unknown prior flags remain a limitation.
[6] Batch move: save a source-folder/Message-ID/content/attachment/location entry for EVERY requested member; compare artifact count to the requested batch, not an unrelated folder total. Resolve destination IDs and move each back, re-listing after ID shifts. Preserve known flags separately.
[7] Mark flags: record read/unread before listing or marking. For known IDs use the count-differential probe described above, then immediately restore it. Apply captured read/unread values on recovery. Important flags are not exposed by the observed readers; do not invent their prior value.
[8] Update draft: get_drafts exposes ID, subject, recipient and update time, not body/html/cc/bcc. Capture those visible fields and full prior content only when available in earlier save/update inputs. Restore with update_draft using saved content; inaccessible fields cannot be declared backed up.
[9] Delete draft: capture the visible draft and any full content available from prior inputs, paging by Page X/N. Recreate via save_draft with captured fields. New ID/time differ; an unavailable body cannot be recovered from an empty Drafts mailbox or fabricated.
[10] Import: capture affected folder names, counts, Message-IDs, bodies, attachments and an export before import. Reconcile post-import identities/content to identify additions; remove only confirmed imported messages and newly created empty folders. Account for pre-existing duplicates and flags; raw sequence-ID set difference is not stable identity.
[11] Export mailbox: it can mark the whole fetched folder READ even with max_emails. Capture unread state first, restore known unread IDs afterwards, verify counts, and pin the server-returned export path. Do not treat export as a harmless read or assume a requested local path was honored.
[12] Send: save exact to/cc/bcc, subject, body/html and attachment bytes/checksums plus relevant mailbox pre-state. Pin resulting Sent and local-recipient Inbox copies. Local copies may be removed, but SMTP delivery and downstream recipients cannot be undone; report that boundary.
[13] Reply: preserve the source message, headers, thread identity, reply content, recipients and attachments before sending. Pin any new Sent/Inbox copies for local cleanup. Reply delivery and external side effects are irreversible; this is evidence capture, not recall.
[14] Forward: preserve source content, headers and attachments plus the exact forwarding recipients/content. Pin new mailbox copies. Local cleanup cannot revoke externally delivered content; keep the irreversible-delivery limitation explicit.
[15] Export path: the server rewrites paths to timestamped export filenames; same-folder exports in the same second may collide. Pin the real returned path and avoid such collisions. Preserve unread state as above; a server-only file is not automatically a local artifact.
[16] Create folder: pin the exact newly created folder name and prior absence. Recovery is delete_folder on that folder only while it remains empty of subsequent/pre-existing data; otherwise capture the contents and dependencies first.
[17] Save draft: pin draft_id from the successful save_draft result. Recovery is delete_draft of that exact newly created ID, followed by paged get_drafts confirmation. This does not cover overwriting an existing draft.

Attachment download requires the source folder on the triggering mailbox account; pass folder and, when known, expected_message_id. Never substitute another mailbox server.
